sources.entry: ColorSet - ColorSet is a macOS utility and framework allowing developers to manage custom interface colors with ease.

summary.one_liner: ColorSet is a macOS app and Swift framework (ColorSetKit) for managing custom interface colors that adapt to light and dark mode.
summary.what_it_does: The ColorSet macOS application lets you create .colorset files containing named colors, each with an optional dark-mode variant, similar to Asset Catalog colors. The ColorSetKit Swift framework loads these files, by default looking for Colors.colorset in the app bundle. Developers retrieve colors by name with NSColor.colorFromColorSet("Name"), and the returned color matches the current UI theme. The README says this is meant to support custom drawing code and macOS versions older than 10.13, where Asset Catalog colors are unavailable. It advises not to cache color objects in custom drawing code, but to call the method on each redraw so the correct color is used after a theme change.
use_cases: Custom dark mode colors in macOS apps
Supporting dark mode on macOS 10.12 and earlier
Replacing hard-coded NSColor values with theme-aware colors
Managing named interface colors outside Asset Catalogs
Custom drawing code that must follow system appearance
notable: Provides an Asset Catalog-like color system for pre-10.13 macOS targets
Ships both a GUI editor app and a retrieval framework (ColorSetKit)
Colors resolved at draw time via colorFromColorSet, matching the current light or dark theme
caveats: Targets macOS only; the README describes only macOS and AppKit usage
Setup and installation steps are not described in the README
